docs.title: FastAPI Observer
docs.text: FastAPI Observer provides structured logging building blocks for FastAPI projects.

docs.title: Current scope
docs.text:
• Typed and validated configuration via ObserverConfig
  • Structured event model via LogEvent
  • Logger factory with console/file handlers and JSON/text formatting
  • Optional in-memory, JSONL, and SQLite event storage
  • Minimal dashboard helpers for inspecting captured events

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
• Python: 3.10 to 3.14
  • Test matrix: py310, py311, py312, py313, py314 via tox and GitHub Actions

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
pip install fastapi-inspector

See Installation for development, docs, and test commands.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Exclude noisy endpoints such as /health and /metrics
  • Redact secrets in both headers and bodies
  • Keep max_body_bytes small enough to avoid logging large payloads
  • Use SQLiteEventStore or JsonFileEventStore when you want to inspect events after the request finishes
  • Close long-lived stores explicitly when a process shuts down
  • Start with log_format="json" if logs will be shipped to another system

docs.title: Recommended baseline
docs.text:
from fastapi_inspector import ObserverConfig

config = ObserverConfig(
    exclude_paths=["/health", "/metrics"],
    redact_headers={"authorization", "cookie"},
    redact_fields={"password", "token", "secret"},
)

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: ObserverConfig controls request selection, output handlers, body capture, and redaction.

docs.title: Key fields
docs.text:
• enabled: turn the middleware on or off
  • handlers: choose console and/or file
  • file_path: required when file is enabled
  • log_format: json or text
  • include_paths / exclude_paths: route filtering
  • exclude_methods: skip methods such as OPTIONS
  • log_request_body / log_response_body: capture payloads
  • max_body_bytes: cap body capture size
  • redact_headers / redact_fields: sensitive-data masking
  • correlation_id_header: header used for request correlation

docs.title: Path matching
docs.text:
Paths are normalized before matching:

  • api/items becomes /api/items
  • trailing slashes are removed, except for the root path

include_paths is evaluated first. If the request path does not match any include rule, it is skipped. Then exclude_paths is applied.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from fastapi_inspector import ObserverConfig

config = ObserverConfig(
    handlers=["console", "file"],
    file_path="logs/api.log",
    include_paths=["/api"],
    exclude_paths=["/api/internal"],
    redact_fields={"password", "token"},
)

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text: build_dashboard_app() creates a small FastAPI application for inspecting stored events.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• / renders an HTML dashboard
  • /events returns structured event data
  • DELETE /events clears the store
  • /health reports service health

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
The dashboard works with any object that implements the EventStore protocol.

from fastapi_inspector.dashboard import build_dashboard_app
from fastapi_inspector.storage import InMemoryEventStore

app = build_dashboard_app(InMemoryEventStore())

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The dashboard is intentionally lightweight
  • It is useful for local inspection and test fixtures
  • For persistent dashboards, use JsonFileEventStore or SQLiteEventStore

docs.title: Handlers
docs.text: The package currently ships with console and file logging handlers.

docs.title: Console handler
docs.text: build_console_handler(formatter) returns a standard logging.StreamHandler configured with the provided formatter.

docs.title: File handler
docs.text:
build_file_handler(config, formatter) returns a rotating file handler.

  • config.file_path is required
  • config.file_max_bytes controls rotation size
  • config.file_backup_count controls retained backups

docs.title: Handler order
docs.text:
build_handlers(config, formatter) preserves the order from config.handlers.

from fastapi_inspector import ObserverConfig
from fastapi_inspector.handlers import build_handlers
from fastapi_inspector.formatters import JsonFormatter

config = ObserverConfig(handlers=["file", "console"], file_path="logs/api.log")
handlers = build_handlers(config, JsonFormatter())

docs.title: From a plain FastAPI app
docs.text:
1. Add ObserverMiddleware
  2. Start with the default ObserverConfig
  3. Enable request or response body capture only when you need it
  4. Add filters to reduce log noise

docs.title: Existing loggers
docs.text: If your app already configures logging, use build_logger() to create a dedicated observer logger and keep propagation disabled.

docs.title: Storage-backed setups
docs.text:
• Use JsonFileEventStore for a simple local trail
  • Use SQLiteEventStore when you need queryable persistence
  • Use InMemoryEventStore for tests and ephemeral dashboards

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
Add the middleware to a FastAPI app and choose the logging behavior through ObserverConfig.

from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi_inspector import ObserverConfig, ObserverMiddleware

app = FastAPI()

config = ObserverConfig(
    log_request_body=True,
    log_response_body=True,
    exclude_paths=["/health", "/metrics"],
)

app.add_middleware(ObserverMiddleware, config=config)

docs.title: What gets captured
docs.text:
• Request method and path
  • Status code and duration
  • Correlation ID
  • Headers and metadata
  • Optional request and response bodies

docs.title: Minimal example
docs.text:
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi_inspector import ObserverConfig, ObserverMiddleware

app = FastAPI()
app.add_middleware(ObserverMiddleware, config=ObserverConfig())
